description.en-US: The return this line belongs to. A line has no life outside its return, which is why it is reached through the return rather than listed on its own.

The original order line whose goods are coming back. Unique within the return: one order line appears at most once per return, so returning the same line twice means two returns, each with its own quantity checked against what is still returnable.
How much of the original line is coming back. Checked against the returnable maximum at creation (BR 55, D-32) and immutable afterwards: changing it would move money without re-running that check.

What this line's returned quantity is worth, taken from the amounts it HISTORICALLY carried rather than any current price (BR 60). A line that was discounted comes back at its discounted share: BR 61's worked example is that a 60,000 line carrying 12,000 of a voucher refunds 48,000, not 60,000.

The tax inside this line's refund, carried separately because the fiscal adjustment needs the tax broken out per line (BR 62) and re-deriving it from a rate would disagree with what was originally charged.

Whether these goods physically come back. False for a service or non-stocked line, which is what lets such a return complete on the refund alone (D-32). Resolved when the return is created and frozen here, so a later change to the product master cannot alter what an in-flight return expects.
